input.reason: zip-bomb style declared ratio, e.g. a highly-compressible repeated-byte payload

expected.check_performed_against: central directory's declared uncompressed size per entry and in total, before decompressing
expected.error_category: extraction limit exceeded: total uncompressed size

notes: D-006 correction, not oracle parity. MSC 1's unzip -o (line 718-719) has no size ceiling of any kind -- it will decompress whatever the archive claims, up to whatever fills the disk, and a slot archive is exactly the kind of file that can arrive via import-from-external-ZIP (createSlotFromZIP, line 1008) with no prior trust established. Phase 6 checks each entry's declared uncompressed size and the archive's total declared uncompressed size against a fixed limit using the zip's own central directory metadata -- before decompressing a single byte -- and refuses the whole extraction if either is exceeded, rather than decompressing partway and running out of disk mid-activation with the current world already removed (the same partial-state risk characterized in world-mutations' activate-extraction-failure-leaves-partial-state-for-safety-backup-recovery, but caused by an oversized archive instead of a corrupt one).
